name: har_oneshot_v1
status: DRAFT for the research-reviewer. Nothing in it has been run, and no session on or after 2023-03-01 has been loaded, read, computed on or printed by its author. It binds only once merged; the evaluation may not be run before the merge, and the sha256 of the merged file is recorded with the run.
relation: the one-shot out-of-sample evaluation that docs/ML_PHASE0.md (tier T1b) and docs/ML_RESEARCH_PLAN.md (M1) promised for the locked HAR model of vol_forecast_v1 (spec sha256 f2d4d047ee19a607b539eda60d187f1b35ad02f1e42f6025a0cfa6b79b74e637). That spec's own lock (2019-01-01 to 2023-02-28) is spent and is not reopened, re-read for a decision or re-tested here; this spec reads from it only its candidates, its loss, its test and its committed dev-period numbers (for the power paragraph).
dataset: the owner's Kaggle source debashis74017/nifty-50-minute-data (version 18), imported by P0.2 as dataset ml-intake-2-feae259bdba6, digest 47d28d6376ca63af (as recorded in docs/EXTERNAL_DATA.md), tier T1b, status external_unverified; use: regime_research. The run refuses a dataset whose digest does not start with 47d28d6376ca63af, and refuses to read it unless told to accept an unverified status. The aeron7 import ends in Feb 2023 and cannot supply the window, so training and test both come from this one source (no mixing of sources inside a fit).
data_tier_limitation: P0.6 (the independent check of the 2023 to 2026 index minutes) is NOT done. The window is read from a dataset that is external_unverified, so every output of this study is labelled 'evidence: external_unverified (underlying only, P0.6 not done)' in its file, its markdown header and anywhere it is quoted. It can support research only: a decision to keep or retire the model as a research candidate, and the planning of later work. It cannot support a live change, a promotion, a paper-gate step, an option-strategy claim or a profitability claim. The label is not changed by recomputation: if P0.6 later verifies the dataset (a verification.json naming the same digest) the result is upgraded only by a dated note that cites it; if P0.6 rejects the dataset the result is void. Between the cross-source test of docs/data/INTAKE_2026-10-24.md (realised variance per session within 10% for 99.7% of sessions in 2015 to Feb 2023) and this study there is no check of the Mar 2023 to May 2026 stretch itself: a source defect in that stretch would be scored as model error.
not_for: no option prices: nothing here qualifies an option strategy, a DTE change, a paper gate, a promotion, a live change or a profitability claim
question: does the locked HAR model (C_har), frozen at 2023-02-28, still forecast the realised variance of the next 30m / 60m / 120m / to the close better than the desk's VolForecaster (A_desk) on 1 Mar 2023 to 15 May 2026, which nobody has scored

window.note: the reserved window of quantdesk/ml/build.py (RESERVED_FROM) to the last session the dataset holds; 15 May to early Sep 2026 is a hole in the data and outside this spec; later sessions (the desk's own tape, a filled hole) need a new spec

decision_points: every 15 minutes from 09:30 to 15:00 IST (volstudy.DECISIONS), exactly as vol_forecast_v1
target: realised variance over (t, t+h]: the sum of squared 1-minute log returns; for 'close' to the 15:29 bar (volstudy.rows, unchanged); horizons 30m, 60m, 120m, close

frozen_model.which: C_har, the candidate vol_forecast_v1 selected on dev for all four horizons and that passed its lock in all 8 cells (docs/prereg/results/vol_forecast_v1-f2d4d047ee19.md)
frozen_model.definition: volstudy.fit_c / predict_c unchanged: per horizon, OLS of log realised variance on log F_B, log previous session's RV, log previous 5 sessions' mean RV, log of today's deseasonalised RV so far and |overnight gap|, with the smearing factor mean(exp(residual)); F_B is A on returns divided by the minute-of-day profile; A and B as in vol_forecast_v1
frozen_model.profile_rule: the minute-of-day variance profile is fitted once, by build.fit_profile, on the sessions up to and including 2023-02-28 and no later (build_tables(profile_end='2023-02-28'); that date is one day before RESERVED_FROM, so build_tables accepts it and allow_reserved_profile stays False). Every training row has in_profile True and no scored row has
frozen_model.training: all sessions of the dataset from its first (2015-01-09) to 2023-02-28 inclusive, the rows with in_profile True. Training stops at the profile's end: the same sessions fit the profile and the OLS, and split.check_test_mask must hold (no scored row in the training set)
frozen_model.frozen: fitted once, before any window row is scored; the coefficients, smearing factors and the profile are written to the result file and not refitted, updated or re-selected inside or after the window. No hyper-parameter, feature, horizon or candidate is chosen on the window
frozen_model.deviation_from_the_lock: vol_forecast_v1 fitted its lock on its dev years (2010 to 2018) of the aeron7 source. This evaluation refits on 2015 to 2023-02-28 of the Kaggle source (which includes the spent lock years 2019 to Feb 2023), because the window must be scored by a model fitted on the same source and on everything that precedes it (ML_PHASE0 rule 1: train, freeze, then grade forward). The structure and the selection of C_har are the locked ones; the coefficients are new.

candidates.A_desk: the desk's VolForecaster without IV: EWMA (half-life 30 min) of today's 1-minute squared returns blended with the prior 5 sessions' mean with weight n/(n+60); horizon variance = per-minute variance x minutes. Nothing is fitted
candidates.B_seasonal: A computed on returns divided by the minute-of-day profile fitted to 2023-02-28; horizon variance = deseasonalised per-minute variance x the sum of the profile over the horizon's minutes

baselines: A_desk is the baseline of the primary test (it is what the desk runs). B_seasonal is the other candidate already in the study and is the baseline of the secondary, descriptive comparison. No new candidate, no other baseline, no model added after registration
loss: QLIKE = RV/F - log(RV/F) - 1 (volstudy.qlike, floor 1e-12), averaged per day over that day's decision points and horizon rows, then over days (volstudy.daily_loss / score), unchanged

primary_test.statement: for each symbol and each horizon, H0: C_har's mean daily QLIKE is not lower than A_desk's; H1: it is lower
primary_test.statistic: d_t = daily QLIKE of A_desk minus daily QLIKE of C_har on session t of the window; Diebold-Mariano t = nw_t(d) with Newey-West, 5 lags (autolearn.prereg.nw_t, Bartlett weights, the rule of vol_forecast_v1); one-sided p = 1 - Phi(t) (normal), as the locked study
primary_test.cells: NIFTY x {30m, 60m, 120m, close} and BANKNIFTY x {30m, 60m, 120m, close}: 8 cells
primary_test.family: these 8 cells are the whole family of confirmatory tests; no other p-value in the result decides anything
primary_test.correction: Holm-Bonferroni across the 8 one-sided p-values, familywise error 0.05 (valid under any dependence, which matters because the two indices and the four horizons are strongly correlated). A cell passes when its Holm-adjusted p is below 0.05. This is stricter than vol_forecast_v1, which tested each cell at an uncorrected 0.05; the change is deliberate, because the family here is the whole claim

secondary_descriptive: reported, never decisive, outside the family and carrying no correction: the same Diebold-Mariano of C_har against B_seasonal per cell (the question of whether the HAR layer adds anything beyond the seasonal profile); B against A; QLIKE, log-forecast-error bias and the move ratio by time-of-day bucket (volstudy.score) per candidate; the cells split by calendar year of the window; the Newey-West t at 10 and 20 lags; the daily loss differences' autocorrelations. A secondary result that disagrees with the primary one does not change the verdict; it is stated beside it

pass_fail.PASS: all 8 cells pass (Holm-adjusted one-sided p < 0.05 for C_har against A_desk) and in each cell C_har's mean daily QLIKE is lower than A_desk's
pass_fail.MIXED: one to three cells do not pass and none of the 8 has a mean QLIKE for C_har at or above A_desk's. Reported cell by cell; the model is neither confirmed nor retired
pass_fail.KILL: four or more cells do not pass, or any cell has C_har's mean daily QLIKE at or above A_desk's. See kill_rule
pass_fail.FAIL: MIXED or KILL: anything that is not PASS
pass_fail.meaning_of_pass: the HAR model, fitted as stated and frozen, beat the desk's present forecaster out of sample on this window and this unverified source in every index and horizon. It does not say that the HAR layer improves on the seasonal profile (that is the secondary comparison, which is weakly powered, see power), and it does not touch option plans. Its only consequence is that the model may be carried forward as an offline research candidate for M1 and for the desk's realised-volatility input pending P0.6 and a separate reviewed change

kill_rule: on KILL the locked HAR model is retired as a candidate to replace the desk's realised-variance input: it is not re-tuned, re-fitted or re-selected on this window, the window is not used to look for a better model, and any successor needs a new spec and data nobody has scored (the desk's own tape from Oct 2026 on, T2). A MIXED or KILL outcome is written up as such, with every cell, in the same file as a PASS would be. The result is not softened by a secondary analysis, a different correction, a subset of years or a re-run

looks.rule: exactly one evaluation of the window. The run writes a marker file immediately before any loss is computed and refuses to start if the marker or a result file for this spec's hash already exists; the result is written once, atomically, at the end. The lock is never reopened for this spec
looks.crash: a crash after the marker that wrote no number anywhere counts as nothing seen: the cause is fixed in code only (the spec is unchanged), the fix and both attempts are stated in the result, and only the second run's output is published. Any number having been displayed or written spends the look
looks.no_peeking: before the run, the window's data are touched only by the preflight below, which prints counts and dates and no price, return, variance or loss; rehearsal of the code uses synthetic data and the spent period (profile_end 2022-02-28, scored 2022-03-01 to 2023-02-28), never the window

sessions_and_gaps.principle: no session or row is dropped, kept or reweighted because of its outcome. Every exclusion below is decided from the calendar and the missing-minute mask alone, before any return, variance or loss of the window is computed, is applied identically to A_desk, B_seasonal and C_har, and is listed in full in the result with the count of rows it removed. Large-move days stay in
sessions_and_gaps.grid: every session the dataset holds for the symbol in the window, as the importer accepted it. Sessions the importer sent to its review queue (a one-minute move above 5% and similar validity flags) are excluded by default in that dataset and stay excluded: the dataset digest pins the decision, none is reopened or taken after this registration, and their dates are listed in the result. This is a known bias toward calmer days (see power and limits)
sessions_and_gaps.locked_rules_unchanged: the study's own losses apply as in vol_forecast_v1: the first 5 sessions of a series and the 5 after any break longer than 4 days have no rows (features need 5 prior consecutive sessions); a (day, decision, horizon) row whose label window has more than 20% of its minutes missing is dropped (volstudy.rows, miss_frac). The last session in the data (15 May 2026) is cut off before the close, so its late-day and 'close' rows fall under the 20% rule. These are mask and calendar rules, but the 20% rule looks at the label window, so a feed outage that coincides with a volatile stretch would be dropped; that is stated, not repaired
sessions_and_gaps.leading_gap: a session with no bar at the open is a leading-gap session: volstudy.grid back-fills its first returns from a later close, which puts the future into that session's first returns and into the next 5 sessions' priors. The build.py guard (build_tables refuses it unless allow_leading_gap) stays on; the platform run therefore does a preflight, from the mask only, that lists the leading-gap sessions of the whole grid, training years included. Each such session and the 5 sessions that follow it are excluded from scoring and from the OLS fit, and the leading-gap session itself from the profile fit, for all candidates. If the preflight finds none, nothing is excluded. The locked run included 5 such sessions per index in its development years and never quantified their effect; this spec does not repeat that
sessions_and_gaps.unit: a session is the unit (ML_PHASE0 rule 3): the primary test is on daily losses, one per session per symbol

power: Planning numbers from vol_forecast_v1's committed DEVELOPMENT folds only (2013 to 2018, six yearly out-of-sample folds per symbol and horizon); no lock-period or window number is used. The window is about 3.2 years, roughly 780 sessions per symbol before the mask rules (a calendar estimate, not a count from the data). Against A_desk, C_har's dev QLIKE gain was 0.043 to 0.092 (16% to 35% of A's loss) and it beat A in all 48 symbol x horizon x year dev cells; the year-to-year standard deviation of the gain was 0.011 to 0.022. Treating the window mean as the mean of 3.2 independent years with that spread, the standard error is about 0.006 to 0.012, so at Holm's strictest threshold (one-sided 0.00625) and 80% power the smallest gain the test can reliably detect is about 0.020 to 0.041 QLIKE, 7% to 16% of A's loss. The dev gain is 1.6 to 2.9 times that, which puts the power at the dev gain above 99% in every cell; if the true gain in the window were half the dev gain the power would be about 98% to 99% for NIFTY and 87% for BANKNIFTY 30m, but only about 56% to 59% for BANKNIFTY 60m, 120m and close. Against B_seasonal the dev gain of C_har was 0.001 to 0.017 and the detectable gap is 0.005 to 0.030: at the dev gain the power is about 99% for NIFTY close, 71% for BANKNIFTY close and 5% to 11% in the other six cells, so the HAR layer's added value over the seasonal profile is largely undetectable here and the secondary comparison is descriptive for that reason. Limits of these numbers: they use year-level spread because the daily loss differences (which the Newey-West statistic uses) are not in the committed dev numbers, so they ignore within-year autocorrelation and are a planning approximation, not the test's power; NIFTY and BANKNIFTY are strongly dependent, so 8 cells are fewer than 8 independent confirmations; the window is one realisation of the 2023 to 2026 regime (it contains no 2020-type shock, and the review queue removes the most extreme one-minute-move days); a gain below about 7% to 16% of A's loss, an effect confined to one time of day or one calendar year, and any difference between the Kaggle source and the truth in this stretch cannot be told apart by this test. A PASS is therefore strong evidence only about the large, structural advantage over A_desk that the dev folds already showed; it is weak evidence about anything finer.
controls_before_the_run: record, in the run's header and the result, this spec's sha256 (autolearn.prereg.spec_hash), the code commit (clean tree), the dataset digest and status, and the table's identity (ml-build-1-<12 hex>)

rehearse the whole command on a synthetic dataset and on the spent period (profile_end 2022-02-28, scored 2022-03-01 to 2023-02-28, a period vol_forecast_v1 has already scored); a rehearsal result is discarded and never edits this spec
the preflight (counts, dates and masks only) runs before the marker; it prints no price, return, variance or loss
load the table through build.load_table(reserved_spec=<this file>), which records the spec's name in the table's attrs, with allow_unverified=True and the result labelled as unverified

command.run: python -m quantdesk ml oneshot --dataset <path to ml-intake-2-feae259bdba6> --spec docs/prereg/har_oneshot_v1.json --allow-unverified --out <an empty folder outside every git working tree>
command.needs_building: the 'oneshot' action does not exist yet: build.py's reserved window and load_table(reserved_spec=) exist, `ml build/reproduce` exist; `oneshot` is to be added to the `ml` subcommand by a separate, reviewed change that implements only what this spec states and nothing else. Until it exists and is reviewed against this spec, the evaluation is not run
command.behaviour: reads every setting (window, symbols, profile_end, horizons, lags, correction, thresholds) from the spec and takes none from the command line, so the only free arguments are the paths and --allow-unverified; refuses a spec whose sha256 is not the one the reviewer recorded as merged, a dataset whose digest does not start with 47d28d6376ca63af, a dataset not tier T1b, any profile_end other than the spec's, a table folder inside a git working tree, and a second run (marker or result present); writes nothing into docs/prereg/results itself. The result (<name>-<sha256[:12]>.json and .md, with the unverified label, the coefficients and the profile, every cell, the preflight lists and the secondary tables) is copied there by a person and committed, as for vol_forecast_v1
command.does_not: import the live engine, write to a journal, place or size anything, use a secret, train anything that influences a decision, or commit any third-party data

reported: the spec's sha256; dataset, digest, status and tier; the code commit; the frozen coefficients, smearing factors and profile; sessions and rows per symbol and year, kept and excluded by each rule, with the excluded sessions listed; for every cell: QLIKE of each candidate, the daily-loss gain of C_har over A_desk in percent, DM t, one-sided p, Holm-adjusted p, verdict; the secondary tables; the overall verdict (PASS, MIXED or KILL) and the opening time
use_if_passed: only as an offline research candidate for the desk's realised-volatility input, pending P0.6 (verification of the dataset) and a separate reviewed change; its effect on option plans is judged by plan research on real point-in-time quotes, never by this study. A failure, a mixed result or a kill is final for this model and this window
